title: Scalar fact-closure follow-up: paired O3 compiler measurements
scope: Original O3 compiler versus candidate O3 compiler, with the same workload sources and flags. Ratios are baseline divided by candidate; values above one favor the candidate.
publication_policy: Constructed from an explicit field allowlist. Original numeric timing, exit-code and allocation samples are preserved. Private paths, host identifiers, raw logs, command payloads, raw addresses, environment dumps and binary/profile payloads are omitted.

provenance.revision_scope: The revision alone does not identify working-tree candidate changes; the frozen source hashes identify measured inputs.

protocol.compiler_selection: A per-mode toolexec wrapper selects the recorded compiler for both initial binaries and Go count-10 corroboration; distinct compiler tool IDs separate cache identities.

direct_compile_configuration.cache: Direct compiler invocations; no Go action-cache lookup in timed batches.

protocol.timing_order: Baseline batch then candidate batch; no randomized alternation.
protocol.profile_scope: Separate CPU-profile invocations are excluded from primary samples. Baseline profiling occurs between baseline and candidate Go corroboration batches. Function cumulative shares include inline callees and must not be added together.

rss_diagnostic.scope: One unprofiled direct compiler child per mode, separate from primary timing; not a distribution or a whole-build measurement.

compiler_results.status: unscored: candidate standard deviation exceeds 20 percent of its median

encoding_json_retry.note: Five paired calibration attempts were recorded without reaching a stable accepted batch. No primary timing result or speed ratio exists; individual calibration durations were not recorded by the runner.

control_disassembly.scope: The actual measured baseline and candidate runtime binaries.
control_disassembly.interpretation: All four control kernels have identical bytes. Their callers have equivalent instructions after address normalization. The recorded placement delta does not establish a cause for observed timing changes; these controls are not evidence of new instruction elimination.

limitations: The control timing changes are substantial despite identical kernel bytes and equivalent caller instructions. Their cause is unresolved; new-workload ratios are campaign observations, not isolated causal estimates for each optimization.
FixedPointDispatch timing methods disagree, so no improvement is claimed for that control.
The main encoding/json distribution failed the stated noise limit and remains unscored. Its retry failed calibration and provides no replacement timing result.
go/parser is one directly compiled package, with a small observed slowdown and roughly nine-percent timing dispersion. It supports no general compiler-speed claim.
Single compiler RSS observations and sampled CPU shares are diagnostic only; they do not give stable pass-level memory or CPU-cost distributions.
Fixed baseline-first order permits temporal drift. One pinned logical CPU was recorded, but CPU frequency/governor state was not captured.
Measurements target linux/amd64 with GOAMD64=v2. They do not establish whole-application gains, other-architecture gains, an asymptotic improvement or a hardware throughput floor.
This file reports benchmark evidence and extraction checks, not completion of the repository's full regression gate.
